cards.explanation: The answer is all things. John 1:3 says "Through Him all things were made, and without Him nothing was made that has been made." That's the whole list, friends, with no leftovers. Even my cookie planet and every oven on it came through Him.

The answer is True. John 1:5 says "The Light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it." The darkness has not overcome the Light. I know a thing or two about dark places, friends, and I'm telling you, it doesn't get the last word.

The answer is so that everyone might believe through him. John 1:7 says he came "…so that through him everyone might believe." He was a witness, and a witness points at someone else. He's like the friend who says "you've GOT to meet my neighbor," and then steps back.

The answer is False. John 1:8 says "He himself was not the Light, but he came to testify about the Light." John is the witness, friends, and the Light is Someone else. I think pointing away from yourself like that is pretty humble.

The answer is that the world does not recognize Him. John 1:10 says "…the world did not recognize Him." And that's though the world was made through Him. Picture an old friend looking right at you and having no idea who you are. Ouch.

The answer is children! John 1:12 says He gave them "…the right to become children of God…" That's the word right there, friends. I once lived in a drawer with a twist tie, so a family like that hits me right in the mustache.

The answer is False. John 1:13 says they are "…born not of blood, nor of the desire or will of man, but born of God." So the children of God are not born of the will of man, friends. They are born of God.

The answer is the one and only Son from the Father. John 1:14 says "We have seen His glory, the glory of the one and only Son from the Father…" The writer says "We have seen…" so this is glory that was seen, friends. And the glory belongs to the Son.

The answer is True. In John 1:15 John cried out, "This is He of whom I said, ‘He who comes after me has surpassed me because He was before me.’…" That sounds like a riddle, but John cries it out loud and clear. Read it twice if it tangles you up, friends, because I had to.

The answer is Jesus Christ! John 1:17 says "grace and truth came through Jesus Christ." The law came through Moses, Israel's leader, and grace and truth came through Him. Good thing too, friends, because my edges needed a lot of grace.

The answer is that He has made God known. John 1:18 says "No one has ever seen God, but the one and only Son, who is Himself God and is at the Father’s side, has made Him known." That's how we get to know what God is like, friends. Through the Son, plain and simple.
